key_insight: LE-DM improves volumetric PTV velocity reconstruction by dynamically masking moving solids and enforcing boundary kinematics inside the same constrained solve.
engineering_relevance: This enables divergence-free, boundary-consistent flow fields near moving bodies, improving pressure and force estimates for experiments with stationary, translating, rotating, or deforming solids.
method: Build a time-dependent signed-distance mask to label open fluid, boundary shell, and solid interior.
Solve Lagrangian-to-Eulerian reconstruction with incompressibility, particle data, surface velocity, and regularization enforced together.
Apply the same framework to moving and deforming bodies using only a signed-distance field plus prescribed surface velocity.
evidence_signal: Validated on an analytical oscillating sphere, synthetic CFD rising-sphere tracks, and a refractive-index-matched tomographic-PTV experiment; the first-cell error dropped from 14% to 3% of body speed and the measured surface velocity was recovered in experiment.
watch_item: Performance depends on having an accurate signed-distance field and reliable surface velocity, especially near steep gradients and complex moving interfaces.
paper_title: Dynamic masking for boundary-aware velocity reconstruction in volumetric particle tracking with moving solids
